description:
Start an iOS simulator, launch an Android emulator, start a Vega (Fire TV) Virtual Device, or spawn an Electron app and wait until it is ready to accept interactions.
Pass exactly one of 'udid', 'avdName', 'vvdImage', or 'electronAppPath'; it picks the platform.
Use when starting a session, once you have picked a target.
Returns a tagged payload: { platform: 'ios', udid, booted, note? } or { platform: 'android', serial, avdName, booted, note? } or { platform: 'vega', serial, vvdImage, booted } or { platform: 'chromium', id, port, pid, booted } (an Electron app boots as a Chromium/CDP device).
On Android the tool hot-boots from the AVD's default_boot snapshot when usable and falls back to a slower cold boot otherwise. Vega starts the single SDK-managed VVD (~10s). If an Android/Electron boot stage fails, the tool terminates the device it spawned so the next retry starts clean.

avdName.description: Android: AVD name to launch a new emulator from (from `list-devices` → `avds[].name`).

bootTimeoutMs.description: Android/Vega: overall budget for the boot sequence. Default 480000 (8 min) on Android, 120000 (2 min) on Vega. Range: 30000 to 900000.

electronAppPath.description: Electron: path to the Electron app to launch. Either a packaged .app bundle / executable, or a project directory whose package.json points the Electron binary at the entry script.

electronArgs.description: Electron-only: extra CLI arguments forwarded to the Electron binary after the app path.

electronPort.description: Electron-only: CDP remote-debugging port to expose. Defaults to a free port; the resulting device id is `chromium-cdp-<port>`. Range: 1024 to 65535.

force.description: Shut down and re-boot the device even if already running. Ignored for Electron, which always spawns a fresh process.

guestVulkan.description: Android on a macOS host only: boot the emulator with guest Vulkan. Defaults to false: guest Vulkan crashes Chrome's GPU process, which breaks Chrome and Custom Tab sign-in flows. Without it apps find no Vulkan device, although the guest still lists the Vulkan features, so a Vulkan-only renderer such as WebGPU (react-native-wgpu) draws nothing; pass `true` to test one. Takes effect at boot: an emulator already running in the other mode is reused with a `note`, and `force: true` reboots it. A boot snapshot saved in the other mode can't be reused, so the first boot after toggling is a slower cold boot. The `ARGENT_EMULATOR_GUEST_VULKAN` env var flips this default to true. Ignored on other hosts and platforms.

headless.description: iOS only: boot the simulator core WITHOUT opening its GUI window (Simulator.app, or Device Hub on Xcode 27+). The device still streams via simulator-server. The `ARGENT_SIMULATOR_NO_WINDOW` env var (1/true/yes) forces this host-wide.

sound.description: Android only (argent never mutes other platforms): boot the emulator with audio output enabled. Defaults to false, so several agent-driven emulators don't all play sound on the host; pass `true` when the task involves playing, hearing, or testing audio. Takes effect at boot: if the emulator is already running muted, add `force: true`. The first boot after toggling is a slower cold boot (the snapshot was saved in the other audio mode). The `boot-sound` argent flag flips this default to true.

vvdImage.description: Vega (Fire TV): VVD image to boot: the `vvdImage` of a Vega device from `list-devices` (e.g. `tv`).

name: boot-device
